actual_scope: For the inverse of the published 5/5/14 frame-506 elimination, attach one carry digit to each of the 5 scales and 14 shears and count the nonzero digits on one low row.
scope_change_reason: PR #7104 leaves open the intermediate-carry count of an elimination word for S^{-1} on one high row. This package answers that count for the inverse of the published word. It does not claim supplier admission.
bottleneck_link: BIT is the next cap after the selected complex supplier. One row of intermediate carry digits is a finer reading of the same frame-506 route. The predecessor already treats a finite carry constant as lower order, so the count does not by itself move kappa.
stop_rule: Stop after the site bound, the closed form on u(q), and the exhaustive censuses at q=3, 5 and 7. Do not retune an exponent or replace the 5/5/14 word.
evidence: PROOF.md range argument for every odd integer q>=7 on u(q), direct evaluation of the one row q=5, and exhaustive base-q censuses of all 3^8, 5^8 and 7^8 low rows. The selected frontier string is read and left unchanged.

open_questions.question: For which odd primes is the one-row maximum of this inverse word exactly 19?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The site bound 19 is attained at q=7 and missed at q=3 and q=5, so the uniform bound is sharp while the small primes are not.
open_questions.first_step: Run the same base-q census on the domain of q=9, which has 9^8 = 43046721 rows.
open_questions.blocked_by: Nothing algebraic. The q=9 domain did not fit beside the q=7 census in this replay.

open_questions.question: Does another elimination word for S^{-1} emit 48 or more nonzero intermediate digits on one row?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The 19-site bound is special to the inverse of the published 5/5/14 word. A longer word has more sites.
open_questions.first_step: Fix one other explicit factorization of S^{-1} into swaps, scales and shears, and count its nonzero quotients on u(q).
open_questions.blocked_by: PR #4957 does not designate a second return word.
